---
name: groom
description: "Keep affected repository documentation and vault knowledge correct, short and in one place. Use in plots that require it during planned work, at harvest in every plot, or when asked to maintain a named scope in freeform."
---

# Groom

Maintain the documents the current change affects. This is scoped maintenance, not a repository overhaul or a vault-wide audit. The repository's and plot's documentation rules take precedence. Outside harvest, this skill adds no mandatory duty to a plot that does not require it, and it grants no new edit, commit or external-write authority.

Read the changed behavior and its owning documents. Follow the plot's vault context and pointers to notes the change could make wrong. An opened note is not automatically a maintenance target. Keep one owner per fact and link to it from other documents.

Record every affected repository document and vault note with one action, update, cut, merge or move. Name the destination for merge or move. Put this list in `## Plan` for spine work, and in the existing session notes for freeform. Include the paths in the authorized scope. If no document is affected, write `none` and one sentence explaining why. Planning is read-only, and the current phase's authority still applies.

When edits are authorized, deliver the list before proof and review, or before the freeform handback. Replace wrong content in place, remove stale and repeated claims, merge useful detail into its owner and repair direct links, headings and entry routes. Preserve unique decisions and their reasons, safety gates and evidence a pending review needs. Follow the global writing standard. Do not add a second telling or polish unrelated content.

Use the existing vault ledger before opening or editing a note, retain first-touch ownership and update its digest after each write. Determine dirty or foreign status from those ownership checks. Follow the existing named-path commit route at the handback. Never fold foreign changes into this work. Leave protected or out-of-scope repairs unchanged and report their paths and reasons.

Read the result as its user. Check facts against the changed behavior, follow affected links and confirm the owning route still reaches retained content. Run the applicable document, size and vault-area checks. A protected gap is a reported gap, not delivered maintenance.

Reviews check the same list and content. A conflict is an edit that removes a decision with its reason or a safety gate, contradicts a binding document such as an architecture decision record, chooses between two owners that disagree, or touches a protected, dirty or foreign note. Stop before the conflicting edit and before any remote write, retain the notes and ask the operator for direction. A groom edit to an executed instruction, such as a skill, plot or global source, is not routine and stops for the existing review rules before any remote write.

Finalize and close-out remain verification-only in plots requiring groom. Their missing lists and unmet actions stop without repair. The routine repair authority below applies only to direct harvest.

Other document gaps are routine. Within the task's existing scope and authority, harvest finishes them through this skill without a question or an extra report line. Reconstruct a missing list or unjustified `none` from the changed behavior and owning documents, then repair the content. Run the applicable checks and commit eligible named paths with the task through the existing repository or vault route. Keep every consent, ownership, record-recovery, proof, review, acceptance and shipping rule. A repository with no authorized unmerged delivery path is protected from late repairs. The handback names the documents changed or explains why none changed.
